name: Multi-Grip / Swiss Bar Bench Press
description: The Swiss Bar (also called a football bar or multi-grip bar) allows the bench press to be performed with a neutral or angled grip rather than a fully pronated grip. This reduces stress on the wrists, elbows, and shoulder joints while maintaining the pectoral and triceps training stimulus, making it a preferred alternative for lifters with joint pain or shoulder impingement issues.

execution.starting_position: Load the Swiss bar onto the rack hooks. Lie on the bench and select the neutral or angled grip handles. Grip width approximately shoulder-width.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the rack hooks at appropriate height for a bench press. The Swiss bar's design places the grip handles facing each other (neutral) or at a slight angle. No adjustments to technique are needed beyond the grip change.
steps: Step 1: Unrack the Swiss bar and hold it above the chest.
Step 2: Lower the bar under control to the chest.
Step 3: Touch the lower chest and press back to the starting position.
Step 4: Maintain a neutral wrist position throughout.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale and brace before lowering. Exhale at the top.
common_mistakes: Letting the wrists roll or bend during the press
Using too close a grip handle, which shifts load excessively to the triceps
safety_considerations: Confirm the Swiss bar is compatible with your rack's hook spacing before use
Start lighter than your straight bar bench — the neutral grip changes the leverages slightly
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full ROM from chest-touch to lockout.
coaching_cues: Palms face each other — keep them facing each other throughout
Drive the elbows down and in rather than flaring wide
